full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-opposite party is the elected President of the Bogra Chamber of Commerce and Industry. The plaintiff was served with a notice by the Deputy Secretary Ministry of Commerce under section 10 of the Trade Organization Ordinance, 1961 on 9-4-84 to show cause as to why the Executive Committee of the said Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Bogra should not be suspended and the function of the Committee should not be taken over. Thereafter the defendant No.1 petitioner passed the impugned order on 6-5-84 and superseded the present Executive Committee of the Chamber and appointed the defendant petitioner No.2, Additional Deputy Commissioner (General), Bogra as the Administrator of the said Chamber of Commerce. The plaintiff challenged the legality and validity of the impugned order in a suit on the ground that the said order was passed illegally and malafide and prayed for a temporary injunction to restrain the defendants from giving effect to the impugned order. In the application for temporary injunction it has been stated that the Annual General Election of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Bogra could not be held during 1982-83 due to Martial Law Order No.43 of 1982. The plaintiff further asserted that the Annual General Election of Bogra Chamber of Commerce and Industry could not be held due to O.C. Suit No.29 of 1981 and finally the election which was scheduled to be held on 1-4-84 could not take place due to pending O.C. Suit No.77 of 1984. The plaintiff asserted that he is the elected President of the said Chamber since 1980 and the order has been passed illegally and in a malafide manner and he has a good prima facie case for injunction and if in the meanwhile the order of injunction be not granted then he will suffer irreparable loss and injury as he will be ousted from his office. The plaintiff further asserted that in the order the defendant could not show any specific instance of willful and deliberate negligence on the part of the plaintiff to manage and conduct the affairs of the said Chamber of Commerce and Industry. 

 3. The defendants resisted the application for temporary injunction on the ground that the impugned order has been lawfully passed and the plaintiff has no cause of action for injunction and that it is also barred under section 56(d) of the Specific Relief Act and Martial Law Regulation No. XL. The defendants also asserted that the suit was not maintainable and as such the plaintiff was not entitled to an order of injunction. 

 From the observation of the Privy Council quoted above, it is clear that by the ouster clause the jurisdiction of the Civil Court cannot be excluded. This view as expressed by their Lordships has been followed in several judicial pronouncements of this court and various other courts of this Sub-continent. Thus by a mere reference to section 22 of the Ordinance it cannot be said that the suit is not maintainable. The plaintiff has challenged the order of the petitioner in the suit on the ground that the said order has been passed illegally, arbitrarily and malafide. Further the maintainability of the suit will be gone into at the time of full and final hearing. 

 8. I am not deciding at this stage whether the present suit is maintainable or not. The issue of maintainability is kept open to be decided in the suit itself. But as long as the suit is not thrown out as being not maintainable, I do not see whey the opposite party cannot maintain an application for an ancillary relief, like injunction. The right to obtain an injunction is ancillary to a right to file a suit and the only requirement is whether the plaintiff has an arguable prima facie case and whether he will suffer irreparable loss if the injunction is not granted. 

 10. The learned District Judge found that the election of the Chamber could not be held in 1981 and 1982 due to the prevailing Martial Law Order No.43, 1982. He also found that due to the aforementioned pending civil suit the election of the Chamber could not be held after Martial Law Order No.43 of 1982 ceased to have any operation and Martial Law Order No. 58 of 1983 came into operation. The election of the Chamber which was scheduled to be held on 1-4-84 could not be held also due to an order of injunction from a civil Court in a pending suit. The learned District Judge also found that O.C. Suit No.77 of 1984 was filed by one Aynul Hoq Sohel and O.C. Suit No.29 of 1981 was filed by one Abdul Khaleque and that the plaintiff had no hand in filing those suits. He found that there was nothing on record to show that the plaintiff willfully and deliberately withheld the election. On the resignation of 10 members of the Executive Committee the learned District Judge held that resignation by itself was no proof of mismanagement. The learned District Judge found a prima facie case in favour of the plaintiff and found that the plaintiff would suffer irreparable loss if he was removed from the present office during the pendency of the suit. The plaintiff is the elected President of the Chamber and there being no allegation of malpractice and corruption against him or any other office-bearer, the learned District Judge found the balance of convenience in his favour and granted temporary injunction. The learned District Judge has rightly passed the order of injunction on consideration of the cardinal principle which empower the Court to grant injunction. Thus I do not like to interfere with the order of injunction.
